old_text: A run is scored—1st, So often as the batsmen after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed, and made good their ground from end to end.
new_text: 1st So often as the batsmen after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed, and made good their ground from end to end;

old_text: The ball shall weigh not less than 5½oz., nor more than 5¾oz.
new_text: The ball shall weigh not less than 5½oz. nor more than 5¾oz.

old_text: It shall measure not less than 9in. nor more than 9¼in. in circumference.
new_text: It shall measure not less than 9in. nor more than 9½in. in circumference.

old_text: The bat shall not exceed 4½ in. in the widest part; it shall not be more than 38in. in length.
new_text: The bat shall not exceed 4¼in. in the widest part; it shall not be more than 38in. in length.

old_text: Each wicket shall be 8in. in width and consist of three stumps, with two bails upon the top.
new_text: Each wicket shall be 8in. in width, and consist of three stumps, with two bails upon the top.

old_text: The bails shall be each 4⅝in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them.
new_text: The bails shall be each 4¼in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them.

old_text: The wickets shall not be changed during a match, unless the ground between them become unfit for play, and then only by consent of both sides.
new_text: The wickets shall not be changed during the match, unless the ground between them becomes unfit for play, and then only by consent of both sides.

old_text: The ground shall not be rolled, watered, covered, mown or beaten during a match, except before the commencement of each innings and of each day’s play, when, unless the in side object, the ground shall be swept and rolled for not more than ten minutes.
new_text: The ground shall not be rolled, watered, covered, mown or beaten during a match, except before the commencement of each innings and of each day’s play, when, unless the in-side object, the ground shall be swept and rolled for not more than ten minutes.

old_text: Neither a “No-ball” nor a “Wide ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “Over.”
new_text: Neither a “no-ball” nor a “wide-ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “over.”

old_text: All runs made from a “no-ball,” otherwise than from the bat, shall be scored “no-balls,” and if no run be made one run shall be added to that score.
new_text: All runs made from a “no-ball,” otherwise than from the bat, shall be scored “no-balls,” and if no runs be made one run shall be added to that score.

old_text: From a “wide ball” as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as “wide balls,” and if no run be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added.
new_text: From a “wide-ball” as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as “wide balls,” and if no runs be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added.

old_text: If the ball, not having been called “wide” or “no-ball,” pass the striker, without touching his bat, or person, and any runs be obtained, the umpire shall call “bye;” but if the ball touch any part of the striker’s person (hand excepted) and any run be obtained, the umpire shall call “leg-bye,” such runs to be scored “byes” and “leg-byes” respectively.
new_text: If the ball, not having been called “wide” or “no-ball,” pass the striker, without touching his bat, or person, and any runs be obtained, the umpire shall call “Bye”; but if the ball touch any part of the striker’s person (hand excepted) and any run be obtained, the umpire shall call “Leg-bye,” such runs to be scored “byes” and “leg-byes” respectively.

old_text: At the beginning of the match, and of each innings, the umpire at the bowler’s wicket shall call “Play”; from that time no trial ball shall be allowed to any bowler on the ground between the wickets, and when one of the batsmen is out the use of the bat shall not be allowed to any person until the next batsman shall come in.
new_text: No trial ball shall be allowed to any bowler on the ground between the wickets, and when one of the batsmen is out the use of the bat shall not be allowed to any person until the next batsman shall come in.

old_text: The wicket shall be held to be “down” when either of the bails is struck off, or, if both bails be off, when a stump is struck out of the ground.
new_text: The wicket shall be held to be “down” when either of the bails is struck off, or, if both bails be off, when the stump is struck out of the ground.

old_text: If the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the striker’s bat or person—“Bowled.”
new_text: If the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the striker’s bat or person :—“Bowled.”

old_text: Or, if under pretence of running, or otherwise, either of the batsmen wilfully prevent a ball from being caught:—“Obstructing the field.”
new_text: Or, if under pretence of running, or otherwise, either of the batsmen wilfully prevent a ball from being caught:— “Obstructing the field.”

old_text: Or, if the ball be struck, or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands:— “Hit the ball twice.”
new_text: Or, if the ball be struck, or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands:—“Hit the ball twice.”

old_text: The striker being caught no run shall be scored.
new_text: The striker being caught, no run shall be scored.

old_text: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any fieldsman may call “lost ball,” when the ball shall be “dead;” six runs shall be added to the score, but if more than six runs have been run before “lost ball” has been called, as many runs as have been run shall be scored.
new_text: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any fieldsman may call “lost ball,” when the ball shall be “dead”; six runs shall be added to the score, but if more than six runs have been run before “lost ball” has been called, as many runs as have been run shall be scored.

old_text: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the wicket-keeper’s or bowler’s hand it shall be “dead;” but when the bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said bowler may run him out; but if the bowler throw at that wicket and any run result, it shall be scored “No-Ball.”
new_text: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the wicket-keeper’s or bowler’s hand it shall be “dead”; but when the bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said bowler may run him out; but if the bowler throw at that wicket and any run result, it shall be scored “no-ball.”

old_text: If the umpire at the bowler’s end be not satisfied of the absolute fairness of the delivery of any ball, he shall call “No ball.” 48*.
new_text: If the umpire at the bowler’s end be not satisfied of the absolute fairness of the delivery of any ball, he shall call “No ball.” 48½.

old_text: The umpire shall take especial care to call “No-ball” instantly upon delivery, “Wide ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.
new_text: The umpire shall take especial care to call “No ball” instantly upon delivery, “Wide ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.

old_text: After the umpire has called “Over,” the ball is “dead,” but an appeal may be made as to whether either batsman is out, such appeal, however, shall not be made after the delivery of the next ball, nor after any cessation of play.
new_text: After the umpire has called “Over,” the ball is “dead,” but an appeal may be made as to whether either batsman is out; such appeal, however, shall not be made after the delivery of the next ball, nor after any cessation of play.

old_text: The side which goes in second shall follow their innings, if they have scored eighty runs less than the opposite side.
new_text: The side which goes in second shall follow their innings, if they have scored 120 runs less than the opposite side in a threedays match, or 80 runs in a two-days match.
